- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slope or introduce early mean-reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting (e.g., 7-day sentiment average) to dampen noise.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70) after a spike, model often fails to recognize — apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often overfits recent noise — use 10-day moving average or sentiment-weighted median for smoothing.
